newsitem.title: CANADA: CS hopes to apply oil technology globally.
newsitem.headline: CS hopes to apply oil technology globally.

text.p: Canada's CS Resources Ltd, which on Wednesday said it signed an operating memorandum of understanding with Chinese Petroleum Corp of Taiwan, sees the deal as a springboard into international oil ventures, CS president Dee Parkinson said.
"We're saying, 'We've got the technology. What other reservoirs do you have for applications worldwide?'" Parkinson said in an interview.
CS and CPC said on Wednesday they agreed to collaborate toward developing heavy oil and oil sands projects in Canada and other countries.
CS is known in Canada for its horizontal and multi-lateral drilling and heavy oil recovery technology.
The companies, which have yet to target any specific oil fields for a venture, said they expected projects would benefit from CS technology and CPC international oil marketing expertise.
Among CS's trademark heavy oil recovery techniques is twin-well steam assisted gravity drainage technology, which uses steam to make oil deep in a reservoir flow more easily into a well.
Parkinson said the deal would not include the firms taking equity positions in either's existing operations.
"They haven't bought into any going concerns," she said. "We're just setting the ground rules on how we would do business together."

State-owned CPC operates two refineries with total capacity of 770,000 barrels per day and a network of over 1,200 retail stations. The company also has oil exploration and production projects in such countries as the United States, Ecuador, Colombia and Malaysia with total oil production of 30,000 barrels per day.
CS produces 15,000 barrels of oil per day in western Canada.
